title: Memory Concepts
content_html:
Memory Concepts

Concept One‑liner Key sources
Working memory architecture Short-term maintenance/manipulation via central executive, phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad. Baddeley & Hitch, 1974; Baddeley, 2000
Episodic vs. semantic memory Personal events with autonoetic awareness vs. decontextualized knowledge. Tulving, 1972; Tulving, 2002
Implicit vs. explicit memory Unconscious skills/priming vs. conscious recall. Squire, 2004
Autobiographical memory / Self‑Memory System Lifetime knowledge structures organize personal recollection and identity. Conway & Pleydell‑Pearce, 2000
Systems consolidation: standard vs. multiple trace Debate over hippocampal dependence over time vs. persistent traces. Squire & Alvarez, 1995; Nadel & Moscovitch, 1997
Encoding specificity Retrieval succeeds when cues match encoding context. Tulving & Thomson, 1973
Levels of processing Deeper, semantic analysis yields stronger memory than shallow processing. Craik & Lockhart, 1972
Context‑ and state‑dependence Environmental/physiological match boosts retrieval. Godden & Baddeley, 1975
Spacing & retrieval practice Distributed study and active recall outperform cramming. Cepeda et al., 2006; Roediger & Karpicke, 2006
Metamemory Self‑monitoring (JOL, FOK) guides learning and retrieval choices. Nelson & Narens, 1990
Complementary Learning Systems (CLS) Fast hippocampal learning complements slow cortical integration. McClelland, McNaughton, & O’Reilly, 1995
Hippocampal indexing theory Hippocampus binds distributed cortical patterns for later reinstatement. Teyler & DiScenna, 1986; Teyler & Rudy, 2007
Reconsolidation Reactivated memories can become labile and update with new information. Nader, 2015
Sleep‑dependent consolidation Offline replay during SWS/REM stabilizes and reorganizes memories. Diekelmann & Born, 2010; Born & Wilhelm, 2012
Temporal context & time cells Sequences are organized by evolving temporal context; neurons code position in time. Howard & Kahana, 2002; Eichenbaum, 2014
Cognitive maps: place & grid cells Spatial/contextual scaffolds for episodic memories and navigation. O’Keefe & Nadel, 1978; Hafting et al., 2005
Event segmentation Perception parses continuous input into meaningful boundaries shaping memory. Zacks et al., 2007
Pattern separation vs. completion Diverging similar inputs vs. filling gaps to retrieve wholes. Yassa & Stark, 2011
Capacity limits & chunking Limited span expanded by grouping elements into units. Miller, 1956; Cowan, 2001
Interference & forgetting Proactive/retroactive interference and exponential forgetting functions. Underwood, 1957; Ebbinghaus, 1885
Emotion & neuromodulators Arousal/novelty (amygdala, dopamine) gate consolidation and priority. McGaugh, 2004; Lisman & Grace, 2005
Social/collective memory; extended mind Groups distribute memory; tools and environments scaffold cognition. Wegner, 1987; Clark & Chalmers, 1998
Cultural memory differences Earliest memory age and narrative style vary by culture. Wang, 2001; Wang, 2016
Distortion & bias (misinformation; source monitoring; seven sins) Memory is reconstructive and susceptible to error and bias across the lifespan. Loftus & Palmer, 1974; Johnson et al., 1993; Schacter, 1999
